Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 54, verses 1–2:

Discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split. (1) And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, "Continuous magic."(2)﴾

By His words, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ He means: the Hour in which the Resurrection will take place has approached. His words ﴿has drawn near﴾ come from the root qurb (nearness), in the form iqtarabat. This is a warning from God, may His remembrance be exalted, to His servants that the Resurrection is near and the end of this world is close, and a command to them to prepare for the terrors of the Resurrection before it falls upon them while they are heedless and inattentive to it.

* *

As for His words ﴿and the moon has been split﴾:

He, may His praise be exalted, says: the moon was split. It is reported that this happened in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while he was in Mecca, before his migration to Medina. The disbelievers of Mecca asked him for a sign, so he (ﷺ) showed them the splitting of the moon as a proof of the truth of his words and the reality of his prophethood. When he showed them, they turned away and denied it, and said, "This is continuous magic; Muhammad has bewitched us." Thereupon God, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, "Continuous magic."﴾

Reports have come in accordance with what we have said on this matter, and the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have held this view.

Mention of the reports transmitted concerning this, and of the narrations from those among the people of interpretation who said it:

• Basher narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: that Anas ibn Malik told them that the people of Mecca asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to show them a sign, so he showed them the splitting of the moon twice.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, who said: Shu'bah narrated to us, who said: I heard Qatadah relate, from Anas, who said: The moon was split into two halves.

• Ibn al-Muthanna and al-Hasan ibn Abi Yahya al-Maqdisi narrated to us, both saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, who said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: I heard Anas say: "The moon was split in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)."

• Ya'qub al-Dawraqi narrated to me, who said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: I heard Anas say: and he mentioned the like of it.

• Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: "The moon was split in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) twice."

• Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Bazi' narrated to me, who said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik: "that the people of Mecca asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to show them a sign, so he showed them the moon split into two parts, until they saw Hira between them."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, who said: A man came to al-Mada'in, stood up and said: Surely God, blessed and exalted, says, ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split﴾; surely the moon has split, and this world has announced its parting; today is the training ground, tomorrow the race, and the foremost is the one who reaches Paradise, and the goal is the Fire.

• I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words ﴿and the moon has been split﴾: "It has passed; the splitting occurred in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in Mecca, and the polytheists turned away from it and said: continuous magic."

As for His words ﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: If the polytheists see a sign that guides them to the reality of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and a proof that guides them to the truth of what he brought them from his Lord, they turn away from it, turning back denying it, rejecting that it is a true certainty, and they say, in denial of it and rejection of its being true: "This is magic, with which Muhammad has bewitched us, when he made us imagine that we see the moon split into two by his magic; and it is continuous magic," meaning: passing magic, from their saying: "This magic has passed" when it has gone.

In accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, who said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿Continuous magic﴾: "Passing."

• Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, "Continuous magic"﴾: "When the people of misguidance see a sign of God's signs, they say: this is only the work of magic; it will soon pass and go."

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿and say, "Continuous magic"﴾: "It means: passing."

• I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words ﴿and say, "Continuous magic"﴾: "As the polytheists say when the moon is eclipsed: this is the work of sorcerers."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, concerning His words ﴿Continuous magic﴾: "When the moon split into two halves: one half beyond the mountain, and another half went away; so the polytheists, when they saw that, said: continuous magic."

Some scholars of the Arabic language from Basra used to interpret His words ﴿mustamirr﴾ as meaning that it is a form of mustaf'il derived from al-imrar, from their saying: "The mountain has become firm" when it is hardened, strengthened and made solid; and "I made it firm" when I twisted it tightly. He would say: the meaning of His words ﴿and say, "Continuous magic"﴾ is: strong magic.

Basharr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿khashi'an absaruhum﴾: i.e., their eyes are humbled.

The reciters differed in reading His saying ﴿khashi'an absaruhum﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Meccan and Kufan reciters read ﴿khushshan﴾ with a damma on the kha and a shadda on the shin, meaning khashi' (humbled). The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the Basran reciters read ﴿khashi'an absaruhum﴾ with an alif, in the singular, following the reading of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud), for in his reading it is ﴿khashi'atan absaruhum﴾. They treated it, though it has the form of a noun, as singular, since it is a descriptive word and, by the rule of fa'ala and yaf'alu, the singular is used when the nouns precede it, as the poet said:

"And youths whose faces are beautiful, from Iyad ibn Nizar ibn Ma'add."

[The line is attributed to al-Harith ibn Dawus al-Iyadi, and is also narrated for Abu Dawud al-Iyadi (Qurtubi's margin, 17:129). The line is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 317), where he says: when the verb comes before a feminine noun, or before a feminine plural such as al-Ansar and al-A'mar and the like, it is permissible to feminize, masculinize, or pluralize the verb; this was done in this word, for Ibn Abbas read "khashi'an absaruhum." Hushaym and Abu Mu'awiya narrated this to me, from Wa'il ibn Dawud, from Muslim ibn Yasar, from Ibn Abbas, that he read it "khashi'an." He said: Hushaym narrated to me, from Awf al-A'rabi, from al-Hasan and Abu Raja' al-Utaridi, that one of them said "khashi'an" and the other "khushshan." Al-Farra' said: In the reading of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) it is "khashi'atan absaruhum." People then read "khushshan absaruhum." And the poet said: "And youths..." the line.]

So he made hasanan singular, though it is a descriptive of the faces, which are plural.

And as another said:

"He throws the roads with them, riders bearing down across the necks of their young camels, with their halters hanging loose."

[This evidence is also among al-Farra's citations in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 317), that when the verb or its equivalent comes before a feminine broken plural such as al-Ansar and al-A'mar and the like, it is permissible to feminize, masculinize, or pluralize it. Al-Farra' commented on this line: al-Judul is the plural of al-Jadil, which is the halter. So if he had said mu'taridat or mu'taridah, it would have been correct, and mursakhah and mursakhayat. End.]

So he made mu'taridan singular, though it describes the necks, and the plural and feminine are both permissible, as we have explained.

As for His saying ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: the disbelievers in God will say, on the day the Caller calls to the terrible thing: "This is a difficult day." They described it as difficult because of the severity of its terrors and its turmoil.

**Commentary on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿Before them the people of Noah denied; they denied Our servant and said, "Possessed," and he was rebuked (izdujira). So he called upon his Lord, "I am overpowered, so give victory."﴾

This is a warning from God, exalted is His remembrance, and a threat to the polytheists of Makkah and to all others to whom He sent His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, because of their denial of him. God had made it clear to them in advance that if they did not turn back from denying him, He would bring upon them what He had brought upon the nations whose stories are recounted in this surah, of destruction and punishment, and that He would deliver His Prophet Muhammad and the believers who followed him, just as He delivered the earlier messengers and their followers from the vengeance He brought upon their peoples. So He, mighty is His praise, said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Muhammad, you have been denied before these, who denied you from among your people. They, when they saw a sign, turned away and said, 'Continuous magic.' The people of Noah denied Our servant Noah when We sent him to them, just as Quraysh denied you when you came to them with the truth from Us, and they said, 'He is possessed.' And he was rebuked (izdujira). It is the form ifta'ala from zajartu (I rebuked), and the Arabs do this with the root when its first letter is a zay: they change the t of the ifta'ala form into a dal, as in their saying izdajara from zajara, izdalafa from zalafa, and izdada from zadda."

The commentators differed about the meaning of what they rebuked him with. Some said: their rebuke of him was that they said, "He has been driven mad (istuṭīra junūnan)."

Those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and they said, "Possessed," and he was rebuked﴾: He said, "He has been driven mad."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the same.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his words ﴿and he was rebuked﴾: He said, "He has been driven mad."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid regarding this verse ﴿and they said, "Possessed," and he was rebuked﴾: He said, "He has been struck with madness (isti'ara junūnan)."

⁕ Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, saying: And Shu'ba ibn al-Hajjaj informed me, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, the same.

Others said: Rather, their rebuke of him was their threat to him with abuse and stoning, with foul speech.

Those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and they said, "Possessed," and he was rebuked﴾: He said, "They accused him, rebuked him, and threatened him that if he did not desist they would surely be among those who stone." The interpretation of His saying, ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring down (11) and caused the earth to burst forth with springs, so the waters met for a matter already decreed (12)﴾

Says the Exalted: ﴿So We opened﴾ when Noah called upon Us, seeking help against his people, ﴿the gates of heaven with water pouring down﴾, meaning gushing forth, as Imru' al-Qays said describing a rain cloud:

"It came in the evening, the breeze turning it over, then there came upon it a southern gust, pouring down"[[The verse is by Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr, from a poem of eight lines describing a rain cloud (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa, Halabi edition, pp. 110–111). Its commentator said: "Raha" means the cloud returned with rain at the end of the day. "Tamrihi" means it turns it over from behind; its root is from "marā al-dar'", which is stroking the udder with the hand so that it yields milk. When the cold Saba wind strikes the cloud, it gathers and thickens and falls as rain. Then the southern winds, according to them, came laden with rain from the Indian Sea, adding to this cloud another southern gust, so the rain multiplied and poured down in torrents. End of quote. The point of evidence in the verse is that "munhamir" in the Exalted's saying "with water pouring down" means gushing forth, very forcefully poured out. End of quote.]]

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said so:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿with water pouring down﴾: "It pours down in a downpour."

The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wil*, the explanation of meaning) of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We carried him upon one of planks and nails﴾ ﴿running under Our eyes, as a recompense for one who had been disbelieved﴾.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We carried Noah, when the water met, upon a matter that had been decreed, on a ship of planks and nails. *Al-dusur* is the plural of *dissar*, and its singular may be said to be *dusayr*, as one says *habik* and *hibak*. *Al-dassar* is the nail with which the ship is fastened. It is said from it: "I *dasartu* the ship" when I fastened it with nails or other things.

The people of interpretation differed on this, and some of them said in it something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Ibn Lahi'a informed me, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, on the authority of al-Qurazi, who was asked about this verse ﴿And We carried him upon one of planks and nails﴾, and he said: *al-Dusur* are the nails.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And We carried him upon one of planks and nails﴾: he told us that *dusuruha* are the nails with which it was fastened.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His words ﴿one of planks﴾: "the ribs (*ma'arid*) of the ship." He said: "And *dusur*: it was fastened with nails."

Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and nails﴾: "*al-Dasr* are the nails with which the ship was fastened; they were driven into it and it was secured with them."

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and nails﴾: he said, "the nails."

Others said: Rather, *al-dusar* is the breast of the ship. They said: It is described thus because it pushes the water and thrusts it aside.

Those who said that:

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya related to us, on the authority of Abu Raja', on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And We carried him upon one of planks and nails﴾: he said, "It thrusts the water with its breast," or he said: "with its prow (*ju'ju'*)."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: al-Hasan used to say regarding His words ﴿and nails﴾: "its prow, by which it thrusts the water."

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of al-Hasan, that he said: "It thrusts the water with its breast."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and nails﴾: he said: "*al-Dusur* is the keel (*kalkal*) of the ship."

Others said: *al-Dusar* are the ship's ribs (*awarid*).

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Husayn, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding ﴿planks and nails﴾: he said: "Planks: the ship; and nails: its ribs."

Others said: The planks are its two sides, and the nails are its two ends.

Those who said that:

It was narrated to me on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿planks and nails﴾: "As for the planks: they are the two sides of the ship. As for the nails: they are its two ends and its roots."

Others said: Rather, *al-Dusur* are the ship's ribs.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa related to us, all on the authority of Ibn Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and nails﴾: he said, "the ribs of the ship."

As for His words ﴿running under Our eyes﴾:

He, may His majesty be praised, says: the ship in which We carried Noah runs within Our sight and view.

It has been reported from Sufyan regarding the interpretation of this, that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, on the authority of Sufyan, regarding His words ﴿running under Our eyes﴾, he says: "by Our command." ﴿as a recompense for one who had been disbelieved﴾.

The people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is that We did this as a reward for the one who had been disbelieved (*kufir*) in it, meaning: who disbelieved in Allah in it.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa related to us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding ﴿as a recompense for one who had been disbelieved﴾: he said, "He disbelieved in Allah."

And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa related to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding ﴿as a recompense for one who had been disbelieved﴾: he said, "For the one who had disbelieved in it."

Others directed the meaning of *man* (who) to the meaning of *ma* (what) in this place, and they said: the meaning of the statement is: a recompense for what he disbelieved of Allah's favours and blessings, regarding those whom He destroyed and drowned from the people of Noah.

Those who said that:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿as a recompense for one who had been disbelieved﴾: "for the one who disbelieved the blessings of Allah, and disbelieved His bounties, His messengers and His books, for that is a recompense for him."

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is what Mujahid said, namely that its meaning is: We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water, and caused the earth to gush forth with springs, and We drowned the people of Noah, and saved Noah, as a punishment from Allah and a reward for the one who was denied and disbelieved. For the meaning of *kufr* (disbelief) is denial, and the one who denied His divinity and unity was the people of Noah, who said to one another: ﴿Do not leave your gods, nor leave Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, nor Ya'uq, nor Nasr﴾. Whoever takes this interpretation, the recompense is from Allah, as if it were said: they were punished for Allah and for their disbelief in Him. And if one were to direct it toward the meaning that it refers to Noah and the believers with him, that would also be a valid view, and the meaning of the statement would then be: We did this as a reward for Noah and for those who were with him in the ark, as if it were said: We drowned them for Noah, and for their treatment of Noah, the things they did of disbelief in him.

As for His words ﴿running under Our eyes﴾:

He, may His majesty be praised, says: the ship in which We carried Noah runs within Our sight and view.

It has been reported from Sufyan regarding the interpretation of this, that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, on the authority of Sufyan, regarding His words ﴿running under Our eyes﴾, he says: "by Our command." ﴿as a recompense for one who had been disbelieved﴾.

The people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is that We did this as a reward for the one who had been disbelieved (*kufir*) in it, meaning: who disbelieved in Allah in it.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa related to us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding ﴿as a recompense for one who had been disbelieved﴾: he said, "He disbelieved in Allah."

And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa related to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding ﴿as a recompense for one who had been disbelieved﴾: he said, "For the one who had disbelieved in it."

Those who said that:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿as a recompense for one who had been disbelieved﴾: "for the one who disbelieved the blessings of Allah, and disbelieved His bounties, His messengers and His books, for that is a recompense for him."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 54, verses 27–28:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them, so watch them and be patient.﴾ ﴿And inform them that the water is to be shared between them, each share being attended.﴾

His words, exalted is He, mean: Indeed, We are raising up the she-camel which Thamud asked of Salih from the rock which they asked him to bring forth, as a sign for them and as proof for Salih of the truth of his prophethood and the veracity of his words.

* *

As for His words ﴿as a trial for them﴾:

That is, a test and an examination for them: will they believe in God and follow Salih and affirm what he has called them to, namely the Oneness of God, once the she-camel is sent, or will they deny him and disbelieve in God?

* *

As for His words ﴿so watch them﴾:

Exalted is His remembrance, says to Salih: Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them, so wait for them and observe what they will do with her. ﴿And be patient﴾: that is, say to him: be patient in awaiting them and do not hasten, and wait to see what they will do to the she-camel of God. It has been said: ﴿wa-(i)stabir﴾ [the original is] with a ṭāʾ whose root is a tāʾ, which was made into a ṭāʾ; it is in fact the form ifta'ala from ṣabr (patience).

* *

As for His words ﴿And inform them that the water is to be shared between them﴾:

Exalted is His remembrance, says: "wa-nabbi'hum" means: inform them, that the water is a division between them on the day of the she-camel's turn. That was because she used to come to the water one day and withhold herself (from it) one day. So He, majestic is His praise, said to Salih: Inform your people of Thamud that the water on the day of the she-camel's turn is a division between them; so they would share that (water) on her day, drinking from it that day and storing from it for the day of her coming.

Some people have interpreted this to mean that the water is a division between them and the she-camel, one day for them and one day for her; and that it was said "between them" only in the sense of "what has been mentioned among them," because when the Arabs wish to report the action of a group of human beings mixed with animals, they state the verb in the form of the action of the human group, giving precedence to the actions of humans over those of animals.

* *

As for His words ﴿each share being attended﴾:

Exalted is His remembrance, says: every share of water on the day of the she-camel's turn, and of milk on the day of her coming, is attended, they attend it.

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 54, verse 32–35:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾

He, the Exalted, says: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy, i.e., We have explained it, for remembrance, i.e., for whoever wants to remember by it and be admonished. ﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾ i.e., is there anyone who will be admonished by it and take heed from it, so that he refrains from what Allah dislikes?

* *

And His words: ﴿The people of Lut denied the warnings.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: The people of Lut denied the signs of Allah with which He warned them and reminded them.

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a violent wind,﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed, We sent upon them stones.

* *

And His words: ﴿except the family of Lut. We saved them at dawn,﴾

He says: other than the family of Lut, who believed him and followed him in his religion. Indeed, We saved them from the punishment with which We punished his people who denied him, and from the stones with which We pelted them. "Bisahar" (at dawn): ﴿a favor from Us.﴾ He says: a favor We bestowed upon Lut and his family, and an honor We bestowed upon them from Us.

* *

And His words: ﴿Thus do We reward those who are grateful.﴾

He says: Just as We established Lut and his family, bestowed Our favor upon him, and saved them from Our punishment because of their obedience to Us, so too do We reward those who are thankful for Our favor upon them, who obey Us, submit to Our command and prohibition from among all Our creation. The word "bisahar" is declined (in the indefinite form) because it is indefinite (nakirah); and when they say "fa'alta hadha sahara" without the preposition ba', they do not decline it.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those? Or do you have immunity in the scriptures? (43) Or do they say, "We are a united, victorious company"? (44) The company will be routed and will turn their backs (45)﴾

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to the disbelievers of Quraysh, concerning whom Allah informed that ﴿if they see a sign, they turn away and say, "Continuous magic"﴾: Are your disbelievers, O company of Quraysh, better than those whom I brought down My vengeance upon: the people of Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Lut, and the family of Pharaoh? They hope to escape My punishment and My vengeance for their disbelief in Me and their denial of My messenger. He says: You are in your disbelief in Allah and your denial of His messenger only like some of these nations whose affairs I have described to you, and Allah's punishment upon you descends because of your disbelief in Him, like what descended upon them, if you do not repent and turn back.

As:

Basheer narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those﴾: i.e., than those who passed away.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those﴾, he said: "Are your disbelievers, O company of Quraysh, better than those who passed away?"

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those﴾: "Are your disbelievers better than the disbelievers whom We punished for their disobedience to Allah? And these disbelievers are better than those." And He said ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those﴾ as an interrogation (istanfaha).

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those? Or do you have immunity in the scriptures?﴾: "Your disbelief is not better than the people of Nuh and the people of Lut."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those﴾, he said: "The disbelievers of this ummah."

* *

And His saying ﴿Or do you have immunity in the scriptures?﴾

Allah, exalted is His praise, says: Or do you, O company of Quraysh, have immunity from Allah's punishment, that it will not befall you for your disbelief in what the revelation from Allah brought you in the scriptures, and the scriptures are the books.

As:

It was reported to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Abu 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿al-Zubur﴾: "It means the books."

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Or do you have immunity in the scriptures?﴾: "In the Book of Allah is immunity from what you fear."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿Or do you have immunity in the scriptures?﴾: "He means in the books."

* *

And His saying ﴿Or do they say, "We are a united, victorious company"?﴾

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: Do these disbelievers of Quraysh say: "We are a united company, victorious over whoever intends us harm and evil, and wishes to fight us and scatter our company"? Then Allah, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿The company will be routed﴾, meaning the company of the disbelievers of Quraysh, ﴿and will turn their backs﴾: meaning they will turn their backs to the believers in Allah in flight from them. It was said: "the back" (al-dubur) is singular, and what is meant is the plural, as one says "we struck the head among them," meaning we struck the heads among them, since the singular conveys the meaning of its plural. * *

Narrated to us by Ibn Bashshar, who said: Abu Asim and Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, both said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salim, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: This verse was not revealed except as a rebuke to the people of qadar: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar. Narrated to us by Ibn Humayd, who said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salim ibn Abi Hafsah, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar﴾, he said: It was revealed as a rebuke to the people of qadar.

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ziyad ibn Isma'il al-Sahmi, from Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Ja'far al-Makhzumi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Prophet ﷺ disputing with him about qadar, and ﴿Indeed, We created everything by measure﴾ was revealed.

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Every small and great thing is inscribed (in a record)﴾ (54:53) ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be among gardens and rivers﴾ (54:54) ﴿in a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, Omnipotent﴾ (54:55)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And every small and great thing﴾ among things ﴿is inscribed﴾, meaning: recorded and written down in the Book.

Those who interpret (ahl al-ta'wil, the scholars of tafsir, or explanation of the Qur'an) have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And every small and great thing is inscribed﴾, he said: "Written. When God wishes to send down a Book, the scribes (safara) copy it."

* *

His words: ﴿And every small and great thing is inscribed﴾

He said: "Written."

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, from his father, from Imran ibn Hudayr, from Ikrimah, he said: "Written in every line."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Inscribed﴾, he said: "Preserved and written."

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And every small and great thing is inscribed﴾, he said: "That is, preserved."

I was told by al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say: ﴿Inscribed﴾, he said: "Written."

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And every small and great thing is inscribed﴾, he said: "Written." And he recited: ﴿There is no creature on earth but that its provision is upon God, and He knows its place of rest and its place of storage; all is in a clear Book﴾ (11:6). And he recited: ﴿There is no creature on earth, nor bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book﴾ (6:38). "It is only (mufta'al, the form) from sataртu (saṭṭartu), meaning: when I wrote a line (saṭr)."

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be among gardens and rivers﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, those who guard themselves against God's punishment by obeying Him, performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience, will be in gardens on the Day of Resurrection, and rivers. The word "river" (nahr) is singular in form, though its meaning is plural, just as "dubur" (the back, i.e. the backs) is singular in His words: ﴿They will turn their backs﴾ (54:45), though its meaning is plural ("idbar", retreat). It has also been said that the meaning is: the God-fearing will be in the vastness and brightness of the Day of Resurrection, and so the word ﴿nahr﴾ was read as meaning "daylight" (nahar). Al-Farra' claimed that he heard some Arabs recite:

"If you are of the night, I am of the day (nahr),
When the dawn comes, I will not wait."

[[The verse is one of the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 319), at His words, "Indeed, the God-fearing are among gardens and rivers": he said, "in brightness and vastness," and I heard some Arabs recite: "If you are of the night..." (the verse). End quote. In Lisan al-Arab (root n-h-r): "A man who is nahr is one who belongs to the day, by way of attribution, as they say 'amal and ta'am' (ʿamal, ṭaʿam, forms of relative adjectives). He said: 'I am not of the night, but I am nahr.'" Sibawayh said: "His saying 'of the night' (bi-layli) shows that nahr is a relative adjective, as if he had said nahari (of the day)." A man who is nahr: that is, one who belongs to the day, not to the night. Al-Azhari said: "I have heard the Arabs recite: 'If you are of the night...' (the verse)." He said: "The meaning of nahr is one who belongs to the day, not to the night." This verse was cited by al-Jawhari: "If you are of the night, I am of the day." Ibn Barri said: "The verse has been altered. Its correct form is: 'I am not of the night, but I am nahr, I do not travel by night, but I go out early.'"]]

Here, on this interpretation, "nahr" is a verbal noun from their saying: "nahartu anhar nahran" (I entered the day/ I was in the day). He meant by "fa-inni nahr": indeed I am one who belongs to the day, i.e. I am not one who belongs to the night.

* *

And His words: ﴿in a seat of truth﴾

He says: in a sitting of truth, where there is no idle talk and no sin, ﴿in the presence of a Sovereign, Omnipotent﴾, meaning: in the presence of One who possesses dominion and power over what He wills, and He is God, the Possessor of strength, the Firm, blessed and exalted.
